newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money eases towards close, gilts steady.
newsitem.headline: India call money eases towards close, gilts steady.

text.p: Indian call money eased towards the close to in the 10.55-10.75 percent range on Monday after touching an intra-day high of 10.85 percent, dealers said.
Some lending by financial institutions helped ease rates nearer to the close, a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Most of the day's trade were reported between 10.65 and 10.80 with stray deals at higher levels, he said.

Dealers said security prices in the secondary market were steady in moderate trade. "The bulk of today's trade was only in two securities," a dealer said. "A large bank was seeking to switch securities and this led to some action."
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded at a 13.14 percent yield against 13.10 at the weekend, dealers said.
The zero-coupon 2000 stock was traded at 14.15 percent against 14.13 while the 13.82 percent 2002 was traded at 13.90 percent against 13.92, they said.

Dealers said the market for commercial paper and certificates remained dull with buyer and seller quotes not matching. Rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 17.0-19.0 percent range for top-rated borrowers, they said.
